follow100Note: Of every $100 of revenue, $88.02 came from Premium and $11.98 from ads. Direct costs took $70.79 and running costs $22.23, finance items added $0.11 and tax was a $0.11 benefit, leaving $7.20 kept as profit. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

oneTimers: Operating expenses included €59M of 'social charges' — Swedish payroll taxes on share-based pay that swing with Spotify's share price — versus €25M a year ago, and the charges came in €46M above forecast as the share price rose; €58M of the €59M sat in operating expenses.

Finance costs of €72M included a €43M fair-value loss on the Exchangeable Notes as the share price rose, plus an €18M loss on derivative liabilities — largely offset by €52M of interest income and €18M of dividend income, leaving finance items at a net +€4M.
The quarter carried a €14M impairment charge on real estate assets, part of the efficiency actions started in late 2023.

The quarter carried a €4M income tax benefit on €270M of pre-tax income — a -1.6% effective tax rate — driven by recognizing deferred tax assets on the unrealized gain in Spotify's Tencent Music investment, versus a €61M tax expense a year ago.
otherDetail: Finance items netted +€4M — €76M of finance income, mostly €52M of interest income on the growing cash pile plus €18M of dividend income, against €72M of finance costs, including a €43M fair-value loss on the Exchangeable Notes and €18M on derivative liabilities. A year ago finance items netted +€6M.

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Subscriptions — 246 million people paying monthly, up 12% YoY; revenue per user (ARPU) €4.62, up 8% (+10% in constant currency) as price rises outweighed product mix; gross margin 31.4%.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier's advertising business — revenue grew 13% (12% in constant currency) on double-digit growth across all regions; its gross margin rose to 13.4% as music and podcast costs improved.

takeaways.text: Gross margin hit a record 29.2%, up 510 bps YoY, on better music and podcast profitability and lower other costs of revenue. Premium gross margin reached 31.4% and Ad-Supported gross margin rose to 13.4%. Operating income hit a record €266M, a 7.0% margin, versus a €247M loss a year ago — Spotify's second straight profitable quarter.
takeaways.title: Record profitability

takeaways.text: Monthly active users grew 14% to 626 million — 11 million net additions in the quarter, though 5 million below guidance as marketing was recalibrated — with growth across all regions, led by Rest of World and Europe. Premium subscribers rose 12% to 246 million, 1 million above guidance, and ad-supported users grew 15% to 393 million.
takeaways.title: Users kept growing

takeaways.text: Free cash flow hit a record €490M, bringing trailing-12-month free cash flow to €1.3B and the cash pile to €5.4B. Net income swung to €274M from a €302M loss a year ago. Guidance for Q3 2024: 639M users, 251M subscribers, €4.0B revenue, 30.2% gross margin and €405M operating income.
takeaways.title: Cash piled up

verdict: Spotify grew revenue 20% to €3.81B (about $4.1B) and posted a record quarter — gross margin of 29.2% and operating income of €266M, both records — as 626 million monthly users and 246 million paying subscribers each grew double digits, swinging net income to €274M from a €302M loss a year ago.
